sentences.text: A chart covered in unlabeled pencil lines is a puzzle, even to the person who drew it.
So navigators label everything, the same way every time.
The course goes above the line: a C, then three digits, then T for true or M for magnetic.
The speed goes below the line, with an S.
Each position along the track gets its symbol: a circle for a fix, a half circle for a dead reckoning position.
And beside each one, the time, on the twenty-four hour clock.
Here, a boat leaves her eight hundred fix on course zero six eight true, at twelve knots, with DR positions at nine hundred and ten hundred.
Why three digits, even for a course like sixty-eight?
So nobody ever wonders whether a digit is missing.
Zero six eight can’t be mistaken for anything else.
